exposure: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection status (positive/negative by RT-qPCR in urine)
outcome: differentiation of ZIKV-infected pregnant women from others
frequency of ZIKV-like symptoms (fever, arthralgia/arthritis, rash, conjunctivitis)
delivery of a baby with microcephaly
cohort: The study included 650 women attending a high-risk pregnancy clinic in Brazil during a Zika virus outbreak.
finding: Physical symptoms alone did not differentiate between high-risk pregnant women positive or negative for ZIKV, with most ZIKV-positive women being asymptomatic and not delivering a baby with microcephaly.
